name: George Wilkes
role: Machinist and engineer at the slaughter-house
bio: George Wilkes was the machinist at the company's works in Medora; in April 1884 he brought tools from Chicago so repairs could be done locally, and he also judged coal and fixed the Cow Boy's job press. In early 1885 he went to Chicago and, with the Marquis, bought the boilers and machinery for the new slaughter-house, which he installed that spring. He caught a rare large bat at the slaughter-house in March 1885 that was to be sent east for exhibition. He left the company in late July 1885 for his home in Chicago, and in December 1886 the paper reported him running a machine shop in London, England.
